A slowly growing stage is constructed from the proved eventual threshold of each fixed requirement. It tends to infinity, is at most the current stage index, and satisfies its own requirement eventually without a presumed uniform rate.

One model is selected against the full signed union. Separate single-template model existence is not used to infer a common model.
The original master list, arity and family remain fixed across replica counts, finite prefix sizes and scale enumeration. Only the finite scale array and independent global replica-slot arity change.

For every finite prefix the model estimate is derived first for a fixed positive error and fixed finite scale array. The slow selection occurs only after these eventual thresholds are known; no arbitrary growing moment-order or growing-scale pseudorandomness estimate is asserted.
The diagonal models are bounded at every stage, using the zero model outside their chosen quality event. They form one sequence, rather than a different asymptotic sequence for every error.

The final enumeration ranges over a finite template family times positive integers. Every fixed pair occurs at some finite prefix, giving uniform convergence over its admissible inputs. No rate or bound for an arbitrary scale varying with w is claimed.
